paragraphs.source_en: Such painstaking preparations showed that Ieyasu was by no means receiving Toshiie merely in his capacity as a chief councillor. Whether summoning Kamiya Shinano-no-kami or calling in cooks familiar with Toshiie’s tastes, it could only be understood as thoughtful concern for the ailing man. Ieyasu was indeed no ordinary man—he was a man to inspire awe!

paragraphs.source_en: Toshiie felt Ieyasu’s single utterance, “Namu Amida Butsu,” descend upon his heart with the weight of a thousand measures. For all the Taikō’s great achievements in life, was he not just as powerless after death?
